source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Norwalk, Connecticut campus publishes 4 MW of IT capacity, which is half of all the published data center capacity this site has found in the state.

Connecticut has five mapped facilities, but only two publish a megawatt figure, and those two total 8 MW. This campus is the larger of the two. The other three publish nothing, so the state's real total is unknown and almost certainly larger than 8 MW. The published number is the megawatt figure, and everything about how it is deployed is inference.

The campus also lists 168,000 square feet of technical space, but no address, no postal code, and no rack count, so the density of the hall is not stated. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 4 MW of IT load is roughly 100 racks. That figure is an assumption about rack power, not a number CyrusOne reports, and at 10 kW per rack the same 4 MW would support about 400 racks. The only certification listed is SSAE 16 Type II, which speaks to controls over financial reporting rather than to the power or cooling redundancy an AI tenant would care about.

A 4 MW campus is small against the gigawatt-scale builds that dominate AI training. Its significance in Connecticut is a function of how little else in the state publishes a number at all. No power redundancy topology and no cooling design are published on the spec page this site read, so nothing here establishes whether accelerators are hosted at Norwalk or what would have to be built to host them.
